about: The gold tier 3 CT dataset's members: CT studies whose field holds the whole spine, C2 to the sacrum, with a person's annotation (the owner's tiers of 2026-10-27; a machine mask never raises a tier), admitted by the field test of rule version 2 (whole_rule; data/gold3-ct/admission.json). tools/gold3_ct.py reads this file, builds the dataset's index from it and the files it names, and holds it to its shape. Confidential, like the rest of SchwingNet: nothing here goes to a public place.
asked: the owner, 2026-10-27 22:49 UTC: "i want all the gold tier 3 CT data as its own dataset, with a indexable database, an artefact, and anything i need to use it in the workflow, including anomaly statistics, and quality assurance they are true anomalies"
tiers: gold = C2 to the sacrum in one study; silver = partial. 1 = a real CT and X-ray pair with a person's annotation, 2 = the pair without, 3 = one modality with a person's annotation, 4 = one modality without. Machine masks never raise a tier.

whole_rule.rule: A CT is admitted when its field holds C2 and the top of the sacrum, whatever its masks hold. A level is drawn at 200 voxels or more. C2 drawn is in view unless the field's top cuts the level below it too; the sacrum drawn is in view when the field holds 20 mm of it below its top; a sacrum the field's foot cuts short of that makes the end out when the foot-most level above it is cut too, and a border case otherwise. One not drawn is placed from the nearest drawn level by tables measured on the members' own whole spines (the 5th and 95th percentiles), with 20 mm of S1 asked below the sacrum's top. The field is measured over the column, and at the image's own edge where a TotalSegmentator grid is padded. A study at neither end clearly in or out is a border case, silver 3 until a person's look. A level the release does not draw is completed by a segmenter, kept as a machine mask of its own and never raising a tier; names the column skips with no room for a body are a count variant, never a level to add. ENHANCE.PET's verdicts, each study judged once on its repaired mask where it has one, match version 1's tiers study for study.
whole_rule.asked: the owner, 2026-10-28 22:58 UTC (#443's question): "if the full spune is in view in the volume, and just missing a mask or two, that should just be completed using a segmentation software of choice ... i dont think i should leave out any spines that have ct volumes with the full spine in view"
whole_rule.source: tools/gold3_field.py (the rule, its thresholds and checks); docs/research/gold3-ct/ADMISSION.md (every count); docs/research/gold3-ct/README.md section 2 (why)

previous.rule: C2 and the sacrum each hold at least 200 voxels; every level from C2 to T12 is labelled; no space wider than 20 mm lies between consecutive labels above T12. A lumbar label missing or extra never drops a spine (the owner, 2026-10-27 17:10 UTC); an absent L5 is the common case and is reported as a variant, and any other lumbar gap is whole and listed for a look.
previous.source: bordercall holdings/count_enhance_pet.py (MIN_VOXELS, UNLABELLED_GAP_MM, LUMBAR_SPACE_FROM, class_of), the rule of the TotalSegmentator count before it

person_key.rule: <member>:<native id>, one spelling: enhance_pet:0001, verse:verse547 (data/splits/anomaly-holdout.json's spelling), totalsegmentator:<sid>. The split part is data/splits/rule.json's hash of that literal string, as tools/catalog.py computes it, so the spelling decides the part.
person_key.leakage: ENHANCE.PET carries no person id: autoPET's 1,014 studies are 900 persons (Gatidis S et al., Scientific Data 2022;9:601), and Leipzig and Careggi give none at all, so each study is its own person key and a person with two studies may sit in two parts. The risk is at most 114 autoPET repeats; it is recorded, not removed.

members.name: ENHANCE.PET 1.6k (sites autoPET, Leipzig, Careggi)

members.tier_per_study: gold 3 for the 1,557 whole; gold 4 for the 3 repaired (1134, 1283, 1347: names moved by a rule the ribs settle, or MOOSE's rerun); silver 3 for the 37 with no C2

scheme.ribs: left rib k = k (1-13), right rib k = 13 + k (14-26), sternum 27; rib k's own vertebra is label k + 7, so rib 13's own body is the one this scheme names L1 (20)
scheme.canonical: 1-19 stay; L1-L6 (20-25) are canonical 21-26; the sacrum (28) is canonical 27; the hips (26, 27) are background. Never VERSE_TO_CANONICAL, which would make the right hip the sacrum and the sacrum a T13.

members.mask_author: MOOSE drew the masks; a medical student verified and corrected each scan, a second student reviewed the first, and a radiology resident and a nuclear medicine resident reviewed both (Ferrara D et al., Scientific Data 2026, doi:10.1038/s41597-026-07218-y): a person's annotation

licence.as_one: non-commercial, the strictest site binding the set (data/licences.json, scidb_enhance_pet_1_6k)

grid.note: the existing word `fetch aws_enhance_pet_labels` lands the whole ground-truth prefix on the owner's word; held says whether it has, set by the grid session once the vertebra and rib masks hash to SHA256SUMS (docs/checkpoints/2026-10-28-gold3-ct-grid/HANDOFF.md), and FACTS.json says where the facts were read and read again. autoPET's CTs are held as FDG-PET-CT-Lesions (/rs/rs_grp_oschome/go2432/data/tcia_fdg_pet_ct_lesions) but no mask has been matched to its CT yet (shape and affine, the scanner columns breaking ties); Leipzig's and Careggi's CTs are not held.
grid.held_note: the masks were read from the public bucket; `fetch aws_enhance_pet_labels` has not run, autoPET's CTs are on the grid as FDG-PET-CT-Lesions but no mask is matched to its CT, and Leipzig's and Careggi's CTs are not on the grid

members.repair_record: the Claude project's files, folder enhance-pet-repair (README, SHA256SUMS, repaired/<id>.nii.gz)
members.persons: autoPET's 979 whole studies are 865 to 900 persons; Leipzig's 379 and Careggi's 199 whole studies carry no person id, at most 578 persons; the set is 865 to 1,478 gold 3 persons
caveats: The four readers' check makes the masks a person's annotation, as docs/research/enhance-pet-gold-tier-3.md says; the corpus-tiers draft (pull request #420) calls them machine output and is not followed here.
MOOSE was trained on all 1,683 studies with their published labels, so its rerun of the three repaired studies is not independent of them; the ribs are the independent check.
86 UC Davis studies are in Science Data Bank and not in the bucket; they are not members.

members.persons: 374 series of 355 patients; the 18 admitted series are 18 patients
caveats: VerSe draws no sacrum: every admitted series is gold 3 provisional until a segmenter's sacrum is added and the field test's placement is confirmed by it.
VerSe's labellers leave a vertebra fused to the sacrum (Castellvi III or IV) undrawn, so a missing L5 is flagged (no_l5), never read as four lumbar.
Five of the 17 series the records read are anomaly holdout persons and two fold 3 persons of the SPINEPS to FleXray route (data/splits/anomaly-holdout.json): carried, flagged, never trained on.
has_T13 in older records is wrong (18 against 6 by the masks).
Where a series is in both releases, verse20's mask is read and verse19's is set beside it (other_release): 99 series, every one with the same grid and the same levels in both.

series.json, from VerSeFusion's demographics, marks 319 series as in VerSe 20, but the release's node b2wxj publishes 313 masks: verse112, verse139, verse141, verse151, verse251 and verse257 have no VerSe 20 mask and are read from verse19.

members.name: TotalSegmentator v3
members.tier_per_study: by the field test (rule 2): gold 3 for the 151 subjects admitted, 5 of them provisional while a segmenter adds a level; silver 3 for the 1,626 others with part of the column, 1 of them border cases; 162 subjects draw no vertebra and have no row. The release's masks are model output refined by hand, counted as a person's annotation and flagged

grid.canonical: the data root's totalsegmentator_v300, by the definition of held; the grid home's copy is another copy

members.persons: 1,939 subject folders, one person each by release id; the 151 admitted are 151 person keys once byte-identical duplicates share one
caveats: v3 names an L6 and no T13, so an L6 its masks draw is a candidate and a thirteenth thoracic body cannot be named; a count needs a reader from C2, SPINEPS and VERIDAH, or Hofmann's 70 reads.
286 of the 1,924 subjects meta.csv gives an age for are under 18 at the scan (15 have none), whose unfused S1 can read as a free body: flagged (child), never left out.

A subject whose masks are byte for byte another's is one scan under two ids: its row names duplicate_of and shares the first's person. Only s2107, s2109 and s2110 are; the release's notes count 1,935 distinct scans of 1,939 folders, and s1445 with s1446 and s2093 with s2094 share a grid but not their masks, so they stay apart until their CTs' sums show them one scan.

Some v3 CTs are padded inside their grid with slices that hold no image; the field test takes the plane where the spinal cord and the column stop together as the field's edge there (tools/gold3_field.py, image_planes), from the masks, until a read of the CTs records each image's own extent.
meta.csv's ages are not checked against the spine: s1411, s1532 and s2065 are recorded 21 to 25 with a child's column (flagged small_column), and s1776, s1774 and s1839 are recorded 115, 117 and 118.

held.definition: A study is held when its CT and its masks are on the grid under the member's canonical root on the data root (grid.root) and every one of those files hashes to the sha256 this repository records for it. A copy anywhere else (a grid home, the Claude project's files, a public bucket, a thread's container) is a copy, readable but not held; a file whose bytes differ from the record is not held. A member's grid.held is checked (with the date and the job), unchecked or not_held; never true until a grid check has compared the sums.
held.why: Rows name files by sha256, so a study used for truth or training must be the file its facts were read from; a copy outside the data root may move or be cleaned away. data/sources/<source>.json's reach held (on the grid now) says the same at a source's level; this is it at a study's.
held.said: the owner asked for one definition of held on 2026-10-28 (#443's question, answered at 22:58 UTC)

completion.rule: The levels from C2 to the sacrum an admitted study's release does not draw (admission.json, complete) are drawn by SPINEPS from the masks the census already holds on the grid, never re-run and never TotalSegmentator (the owner's science rule), kept as a machine arm of their own beside the release's masks, recorded by segmenter, version and sha256, never pooled with the release's masks and never raising a tier.

auto_anatomist.spines: VerSe, TotalSegmentator and ENHANCE.PET (the owner, 2026-10-28 23:03 UTC: "i meant verse+totalsegmentator+PET")
auto_anatomist.label: a mask per vertebral level, named by level; no member carries measurements
auto_anatomist.why: data/recipes/non-commercial.json allows open, share-alike and non-commercial with no owner review, so it takes all three whole (TotalSegmentator open, VerSe share-alike, ENHANCE.PET non-commercial as one); recommended on the owner's behalf for him to overrule. A commercial network would take TotalSegmentator alone, with ENHANCE.PET's Leipzig and Careggi only after a per-site split and every class first confirmed by the owner, and VerSe only under commercial-share-alike after counsel; loosening a class is the owner's alone.
